title: Joint zero-map detection from finite-stage fibre comparisons
statement: Let k be a field, l a prime invertible in k, R a continuous rational realization family, Ω an algebraic closure of Q_l, and ω normalized finite fibres [def-per-adic-fibre-comparison-data, lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness]. Supply CommonStageHeartExactness [def-per-common-stage-fibre-descent-interfaces]. For each finite-type separated k-scheme X and each geometric point x, let V_x be any CommonPoint for ω: an exact additive finite-dimensional common-heart fibre functor with natural isomorphisms on every finite stage. If a common-heart arrow f:F→G has V_x(f)=0 for every algebraically closed geometric point x, then f=0. No scalar or pullback compatibility hypothesis on the V_x is required.

proof.text: Choose finite-heart presentations of the two endpoints, then one finite stage representing the conjugated arrow, using [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations, prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Naturality of finite_stage conjugates each common fibre map to the scalar extension of the finite fibre map. The supplied faithful scalar extension reflects zero. Finite zero-map detection of [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness] then makes this representative zero. Its quotient and the original conjugated arrow are zero. The stage is chosen for the arrow independently of the geometric point; the conclusion also covers empty schemes.
